packet: Finite inverse horizons and small ordinary ancestors
status: Source-qualified written analytic deductions plus a strict Lean check of the finite block telescope; no Collatz closure claim.

new_written_results.statement: If every unit predecessor of q through depth K is at least b and 3^(4m)<=b, then max_{s<=K} D_s(q)/q <= b^(-1/2)+C_A K(K+2)m^(-A-1).
For every fixed B,R>0, sup_{s<=log(b)^B} D_s(q)/q = O_{B,R}(log(b)^(-R)), uniformly under the stated predecessor floor.
The same uniform horizon bound holds for V_k by V_k<=kappa D_{k+1}.
For hypothetical least-unit q with V(q)>=eta q/log(q+2), p_L(q)=O_R(log(q)^(-R)) uniformly for L<=log(q)^B, for each fixed B,R.
A certificate V_k(q)>=eta q/log(q+2) with k<=log(q)^B forces a positive odd unit n<exp(log(q)^gamma)<q, with U^j(n)=q and 1<=j<=k+1, for any fixed gamma in (0,1) and all sufficiently large q.

lean_verification.interpretation: For f_s=D_s(q)/q, base=b^(-1/2), and epsilon=C_A*m^(-A), the checked algebra gives the accumulated quadratic error. The analytic hypotheses themselves are explicit, unformalized inputs.

remaining_gap: No bound yet puts every critical infinite-depth canonical value into a fixed polylogarithmic finite certificate horizon. The actual-kernel drift needed to sum adaptive logarithmic errors has not been proved.
